I also read the downstream uses in ModuleTensorAffine.lean, which use `change`, `exact` and `rw` for these rewrites. I could not run Lean. findings.problem: This is the canonical computation rule for the new definition `stalkMapLinear` on germs. Its LHS is headed by the new constant `stalkMapLinear`, and the RHS is strictly smaller (the map is gone). It is not a simp lemma, and nothing else in the file's simp set unfolds `stalkMapLinear`. Mathlib's analogous rule `stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply'` is @[simp], but it does not fire on `stalkMapLinear`, because that is an opaque def. So `simp` cannot compute `stalkMapLinear ... (germ ...)`. Downstream users must invoke the lemma by name, e.g. via `rw [PresheafOfModulesOfCommRing.stalkMapLinear_germ, hpqmap]` in `stalkTensorEquiv_naturality`, and similarly in the affine file.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`: `@[simp] theorem stalkMapLinear_germ ...`. The rewrite is terminating and non-looping. It does not conflict with `stalkMapLinear_apply_stalkFunctor`, which is not simp and which should stay non-simp. If it were simp, its RHS would compete with `stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply'`. Then `rw [stalkMapLinear_germ, ...]` in `stalkTensorEquiv_naturality` can be replaced by `simp` or `simp only [stalkMapLinear_germ]`.
findings.benefit: Germ-level computations about stalk maps normalise to `germ Q (f.app (op U) p)`, which is the same form Mathlib's simp set uses for `stalkFunctor.map`. This removes manual `rw`/`exact` invocations in this file and in dependent files.

findings.problem: This is the defining evaluation rule of the comparison equivalence `stalkTensorEquiv` on pure-tensor germs. The rewrite is directional, terminating and has a strictly simpler RHS (a tensor of germs). It has no simp attribute. The only way to use it is by name, as in the proof of `stalkTensorEquiv_naturality` and in ModuleTensorAffine.lean, where it is applied via a `change ... :=` plus an explicit call. The statement also relies on `show (P ⊗ Q).obj (op V) from p ⊗ₜ q` to coerce the tensor into the right type. That makes it hard to use with `rw`/`simp` unless the user reproduces the same elaboration.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `stalkTensorEquiv_germ_tmul`. This is the only evaluation rule for the equiv, so no competing rule exists. Check with `simpNF` that the LHS is syntactically matchable. If the `show` coercion makes the LHS unmatchable, restate the LHS with the instance-explicit `TensorProduct.tmul` form that `simp` produces. Optionally add the symm-image `stalkTensorEquiv.symm (germ ⊗ₜ germ) = germ (p ⊗ₜ q)` as a companion simp lemma.
findings.benefit: Downstream proofs such as the `calc` step in `stalkTensorEquiv_naturality` and the affine comparison proof could close the step with `simp` instead of a hand-written `exact`/`change`. This gives users a canonical normal form (tensor of germs) for the equiv on pure tensors.
